# Explanations

Help the reader build an understanding they can use.

Begin with a concrete situation or question, then develop the idea through an intelligible sequence. Use headings that carry meaning, examples that make distinctions visible, and figures that explain relationships more directly than prose can.

Keep explanation near the thing it explains. Vary scale and density to distinguish the main argument from supporting detail, and give difficult ideas space to settle. Let readers follow the whole account or return to a particular point. Choose the depth and pace for what they already know and what they need to do next.
